documents.title: The Policy Process Literature
documents.content:
Title: The Policy Process Literature
Abstract: Abstract The chapter reviews policy process theories such as punctuated equilibrium theory, the advocacy coalition framework, and policy paradigms, and argues that they converge on the insight that policy change is the result of a complex process, which is shaped by large numbers of heterogeneous inputs. These inputs vary over time and issue areas and contain a stochastic element. This calls for a stochastic process model. The chapter presents two prominent stochastic process models, the theory of serial judgment and the dynamic model of choice for public policy. The mixture model of politics builds on this foundation. Thus, the chapter sets out the theoretical foundations for a mixture perspective on politics.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: The Mixture Model of Politics
documents.content:
Title: The Mixture Model of Politics
Abstract: Abstract This chapter develops the mixture model of politics. The chapter defines contributions as all stimuli affecting policy, whether arising from lobbying, demographic shifts, institutional processes, or unexpected events. It argues that a policy adopted in a formal arena is the result of long, distributed, and often informal processes of policy-making involving many and changing participants. The chapter formalizes how policy change results from varying numbers of contributions, each containing a stochastic component. The number of contributions varies over time, and across countries and issue areas. The mixture model of politics shows how such variation in contributions leads to predictable patterns of policy change.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: The Comparative Distributional Method
documents.content:
Title: The Comparative Distributional Method
Abstract: Abstract The chapter introduces the Comparative Distributional Method (CDM) as a statistical approach for analysing policy change distributions. It outlines the limitations of relying on conventional methods such as visual inspection of histograms and descriptive measures such as kurtosis and argues that a formal statistical model is needed for distributional analysis in the same way that regression models are used for analysing relationships between variables. Drawing on a class of distributions developed for mixture processes, the chapter presents the CDM, demonstrates how it can be used to model and compare policy change distributions, and introduces the NIG diamond as a tool for visualizing differences in distributional shapes. It also shows how these models enable predictions about policy changes.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Measuring Policy Change
documents.content:
Title: Measuring Policy Change
Abstract: Abstract The chapter is about how to handle policy change data in comparative distributional analysis. It identifies three central considerations. It shows, using the mixture model, that pooling and aggregation of observations systematically affect the shape of policy change distributions. This implies that data must be treated consistently across cases to avoid biased comparisons. It then clarifies the relationship between politics and policy change, arguing that although policy changes reflect political processes, distributional patterns in policy change cannot be directly translated into insights about individual contributions to politics. Finally, the chapter presents the spending datasets used in the empirical analyses of the book and introduces CDMethods, an R package designed to implement the Comparative Distributional Method.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Mixtures in Danish Defence Politics
documents.content:
Title: Mixtures in Danish Defence Politics
Abstract: Abstract This chapter applies the mixture model to a longitudinal case study of Danish civil defence and home guard policy from the post-war period to the present. It examines how policy change in these two issue areas reflects shifting numbers of contributions, ranging from institutional developments and political conflicts to external events. By tracking how these contributions vary over time and differ across the two issue areas, the chapter illustrates the logic of the mixture model: that policy change emerges from mixtures of contributions. Using the Comparative Distributional Method, policy change distributions from the two issue areas are characterized and compared. The analysis shows how contributions shape policy and how institutional traits of an issue area matter.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Public Spending Mixtures across Countries
documents.content:
Title: Public Spending Mixtures across Countries
Abstract: Abstract This chapter analyses distributions of public spending changes across OECD countries using the Comparative Distributional Method. It estimates policy change distributions for each country and compares their shapes in the NIG diamond, providing a systematic view of cross-national variation. The chapter shows how the mixture model can be used to understand how distributions of policy change differ across countries. Furthermore, using examples from Austria and Latvia, it is shown how estimated distributions can be used to calculate predictions about policy change. A goodness-of-fit test evaluates the mixture model against two alternative stochastic process models. The test shows that the mixture model offers a strong empirical fit with spending data across countries.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Policy Issues and Mixture Distributions
documents.content:
Title: Policy Issues and Mixture Distributions
Abstract: Abstract This chapter compares policy change distributions across issue areas. It begins with a discussion of issue-area typologies and argues that different issue areas would exhibit distinct distributional shapes but that these differences are unlikely to be uniform across countries. Because policy-making on similar issues is organized in different ways across countries, the number and variation of contributions also differ. Using OECD spending data and the Comparative Distributional Method, the chapter shows that most of the variation in spending change distributions is caused by country-level rather than issue-level factors. The findings suggest that the institutional context and national political structures play a larger role than generic issue characteristics in shaping policy change distributions.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized

documents.title: The Pattern of Politics
documents.content:
Title: The Pattern of Politics
Abstract: Abstract This chapter discusses the main findings of the book and the implications for theory and method, and the empirical applications of the mixture model. It recaps the idea that according to the mixture model, policy change is generated by mixtures of many contributions which vary over time and across issue areas. It highlights two results: country-level factors such as institutional arrangements and degrees of democracy are associated with the shapes of spending change distributions, and similar issues do not have similar distributions across countries. It also stresses the importance of data treatment, and how pooling and aggregation affect distributions. Building on this, the chapter discusses three examples of how the mixture model can be applied beyond public spending. The chapter concludes by discussing how the mixture model and the Comparative Distributional Method can contribute to our understanding of the pattern of politics.
Authors: Jens Ledet Jensen, Peter B Mortensen, Søren Serritzlew
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Adaptive-threshold max-SVM model with progressive-iterative algorithm for high-dimensional data classification and feature selection
documents.content:
Title: Adaptive-threshold max-SVM model with progressive-iterative algorithm for high-dimensional data classification and feature selection
Abstract: Purpose Support vector machines have been progressively refined in existing research, but there are still certain limitations in feature selection for high-dimensional data. Design/methodology/approach This paper proposes an adaptive-threshold max-SVM model, which seeks to improve the accuracy and effectiveness of classification and identifies key features. The model comprises a set of SVM sub-models, each trained on a specific feature combination and adjusting its decision boundary with adaptively optimized thresholds. All sub-models independently generate classification results, and the final decision is determined by selecting the maximum value from these outputs. Findings In biomedical data analysis, this model achieves high accuracy with 100\% sensitivity. It delivers superior performance over conventional models in repeated cross-validation and exhibits strong generalization and robustness, which are also validated on non-biomedical datasets. Originality/value This paper designs a novel adaptive-threshold max-SVM model equipped with the Progressive-Iterative Algorithm. The algorithm consists of a three-step screening and iterative construction process that identifies an optimal combination of sub-models from a large candidate pool. It enables efficient feature selection, delivering favorable classification performance, generalization ability and robustness.
Authors: Binyan Xiong, Wangyong Lv, Zhehao Sun, Qiqi Guo
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Effects of periodontal pathobiont infection on a 3D mucosa model
documents.content:
Title: Effects of periodontal pathobiont infection on a 3D mucosa model
Abstract: Abstract Background Establishing 3D in vitro mucosa models replicating the architecture and cellular complexity of human tissues has been an elusive, yet relevant goal to study oral biofilm interactions and bridge the gap between monolayer assays and in vivo experiments. This study reports the development of such a model using primary human gingival fibroblasts and human gingival epithelial progenitor cells, and its response to the periodontal pathobionts Fusobacterium nucleatum and Porphyromonas gingivalis . Methods The cells were cultured in transwell inserts for 28 days with sequential media transitions (CnT-PR-F -> CnT-PR-CC -> CnT-PR-FTAL5; CellnTec, Switzerland). The model was airlifted at day 13 to promote epithelial stratification. Tissue organization was evaluated by histology and immunofluorescence and the barrier function was assessed by permeability assay with 4 kDa dextran-FITC. Bacterial growth conditions for co-culturing were evaluated in co-culture media and in saliva, in tenfold increasing concentrations up to 108 CFU/mL, at two different timepoints (16 h and 24 h), and in anaerobic and under CO2 environment using culturing and optical density measurements. Finally, the co-cultures were incubated with P. gingivalis (10⁷CFU/mL) or dual species (F. nucleatum and P. gingivalis, each 5 × 10⁶CFU/mL) under CO₂ for 16 h and 24 h in saliva. Morphological and structural changes were analyzed microscopically and immune response was assessed for cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα by ELISA. Results The 3D mucosa model exhibited 4–6 cohesive epithelial layers (overall thickness ~ 150–200 μm) with a typical polarized appearance fixed to the underlying connective tissue layer. Minimal dextran-FITC translocation through the model was detected confirming the presence of a functionally intact epithelial barrier. Upon bacterial exposure, epithelial integrity decreased in a time- and composition-dependent manner: after 16 h, the dual-species biofilm caused wider intercellular spaces and partial loss of epithelial cohesion compared to P. gingivalis alone; by 24 h, epithelial disruption was observed with visible bacterial invasion and early biofilm formation. Subepithelial fibroblast organization also appeared altered. Additionally, ELISA assays revealed condition-dependent modulation of cytokines IL-8, IL-6, and IL-1 β, indicating a soft tissue response to bacterial challenge. Conclusions This 3D gingival mucosa model provides a reproducible platform to study host-biofilm interactions using primary cell lines. The time- and species-dependent epithelial disruption highlights its potential for investigating mechanisms of periodontal pathogenesis and evaluating preventive approaches.
Authors: Pearly Perumpallil, Hedwig Wariwoda, Daniel Baumhoer, Maurizio S. Tonetti, Michael M. Bornstein, Monika Astasov-Frauenhoffer
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: DIGREP: a grey-relational deep ensemble model for construction waste prediction
documents.content:
Title: DIGREP: a grey-relational deep ensemble model for construction waste prediction
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of construction waste is critical for sustainable resource management and environmental protection. This study presents a deep integrated grey-relational ensemble predictor model that combines grey relational analysis for feature selection with a stacking ensemble of backpropagation network, convolutional neural network and long short-term memory neural networks, with random forest as the meta-learner. The model integrates generation source attributes as well as material characteristics of construction waste. Experimental results on datasets from Eurostat and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency show that the model achieves a mean absolute error of 5.4 tonnes, a mean squared error below 12.6 tonnes2 and an R2 of 0.913. In addition, it maintains a waste processing response time within 0.8 s and realises a recovery rate of 89.7%. The model effectively addresses multi-source heterogeneity and complex non-linear interactions, offering a robust solution for both short- and long-term waste prediction. These findings support smart waste planning and offer practical value for the circular economy and low-carbon construction.
Authors: Xueshan Li, Baoquan Gu, Xinzhu Wang, Xiuli Zhang, Mengna Zhang, Pengfei Li
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: State and Legal Constructivism in Creation of the Soviet Corporate Economic Activity Model (Trust) in the Period of the New Economic Policy, Carried Out in Russia in the 1920s
documents.content:
Title: State and Legal Constructivism in Creation of the Soviet Corporate Economic Activity Model (Trust) in the Period of the New Economic Policy, Carried Out in Russia in the 1920s
Abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the legal nature of the trust in the conditions of the mixed Soviet economy of the 20s of the 20th century with the dominance of state property. It is established that the organizational and legal structure of the business association, which the trust acted as, fit into the new system of the national economy that arose during the period of the new economic policy and was subsequently transformed into various kinds of national economic sectoral and inter-sectoral complexes. As a result of the study, the author comes to the conclusion that the previously established organizational and legal forms of business associations can be quite successfully adapted to new historical realities.
Authors: Tatyana K. Krasilnikova
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Value Transformations of Modern Russian Constitutionalism and Their Influence on the Constitutional Law Model of Direct Grassroots Democracy
documents.content:
Title: Value Transformations of Modern Russian Constitutionalism and Their Influence on the Constitutional Law Model of Direct Grassroots Democracy
Abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of value and ideological transformations affecting the constitutional and legal model of direct democracy in modern Russia. The author explores the departure from liberal individualistic principles in favor of the concept of a moral state based on spiritual unity, the priority of public interests and cultural and historical continuity. Special attention is paid to rethinking the role of local self-government, which is considered not as an element of the mechanics of power, but as a form of self-organization of local communities. The paper substantiates the thesis about the insufficiency and crisis of traditional direct forms of expression of will (elections, referendums) and raises the question of the need to recognize alternative, corporate and conciliar practices of identifying the will of the people as full-fledged institutions of democracy. The author concludes that constitutional reform and doctrinal re-traditionalization consolidate a consolidated understanding of national unity, calling into question the monopoly of the party system on political representation.
Authors: Sergey S. Zenin

documents.title: CROSS-BORDER TRANSFER OF PERSONAL DATA: MODEL SITUATIONS FOR QUALIFYING CRIMES UNDER PART 4 OF ARTICLE 272.1 OF THE CRIMINAL CODE OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
documents.content:
Title: CROSS-BORDER TRANSFER OF PERSONAL DATA: MODEL SITUATIONS FOR QUALIFYING CRIMES UNDER PART 4 OF ARTICLE 272.1 OF THE CRIMINAL CODE OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
Abstract: The article studies the cross-border transfer of personal data as a qualifying factor of elements of crime provided for in Part 4 of Article 272.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation. Particular attention is paid to borderline qualification situations: transfer to a foreign cloud infrastructure, forwarding via instant messengers with foreign servers, actions of an employee with official access, transfer through intermediaries, and operations with anonymized data. The conclusion is made that the main practical problem is the distinction between administrative offences and crimes in the sphere of crossborder circulation of personal data; a system of qualification criteria aimed at reducing the risk of an expansive interpretation of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation is proposed.
Authors: Georgy V. Gavrilov
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Debt financing and agricultural income among large-scale grain producers: evidence from Jiangsu Province, China
documents.content:
Title: Debt financing and agricultural income among large-scale grain producers: evidence from Jiangsu Province, China
Abstract: Achieving agricultural income growth among large-scale grain producers (LSGPs) is crucial for ensuring food security and promoting sustainable agricultural development. Based on 2022 survey data from 645 LSGPs in Jiangsu Province, China, this study employs ordinary least squares (OLS), two-stage least squares (2SLS), and a mediation effect model to examine the effects, mechanisms, and scale boundaries of debt financing on agricultural income. The results show that total credit, traditional credit, private credit, and trade credit have inverted U-shaped effects on agricultural income, whereas digital credit has a significantly positive effect. Mechanism analysis shows that debt financing increases agricultural income mainly through the scale of transferred-in farmland, machinery investment, and infrastructure investment. Traditional credit and digital credit increase agricultural income through all three channels; trade credit works through the scale of transferred-in farmland and machinery investment; and private credit works mainly through the scale of transferred-in farmland. The effect of debt financing on agricultural income also exhibits educational heterogeneity. Compared with farmers with junior high school education or below, those with senior high school education or above have higher turning points for total credit and trade credit, and the positive income effect of digital credit is more pronounced. These findings suggest that financial policies should promote the orderly development of digital credit, keep debt financing within an appropriate range, strengthen support for productive investment, and provide differentiated financial services according to farmers' educational attainment.
Authors: Pengju Han, Lingjuan Cheng
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

Traditional credit and digital credit increase agricultural income through all three channels; trade credit works through the scale of transferred-in farmland and machinery investment; and private credit works mainly through the scale of transferred-in farmland. The effect of debt financing on agricultural income also exhibits educational heterogeneity. Compared with farmers with junior high school education or below, those with senior high school education or above have higher turning points for total credit and trade credit, and the positive income effect of digital credit is more pronounced. These findings suggest that financial policies should promote the orderly development of digital credit, keep debt financing within an appropriate range, strengthen support for productive investment, and provide differentiated financial services according to farmers' educational attainment.

documents.title: Measurement and dynamic evolution of China’s agricultural new quality productive forces: a study based on the Pressure-State-Response model
documents.content:
Title: Measurement and dynamic evolution of China’s agricultural new quality productive forces: a study based on the Pressure-State-Response model
Abstract: Based on the Pressure-State-Response (PSR) theoretical framework, this study constructs a comprehensive evaluation system for agricultural new quality productive forces (ANQPFs). The entropy method is employed to systematically measure the development level of provincial ANQPFs in China from 2014 to 2023. Methods including the Dagum Gini coefficient, kernel density estimation, ArcGIS spatial analysis, Moran’s I, and geodetectors—to systematically examine regional disparities, decompose their sources, delineate spatiotemporal evolutionary dynamics, and identify the key underlying driving mechanisms. The findings indicate that during the study period, China’s ANQFPs steadily increases, with the regional pattern following a hierarchy of East > Central > Northeast > West. Among the PSR dimensions, the Response dimension consistently plays a core driving role, the importance of the State dimension gradually strengthens, while the contribution of the pressure dimension remains relatively limited. Regional differences first expand and then stabilize, with inter-regional differences being the dominant factor. The kernel density curves show that inter-regional development imbalance is becoming increasingly prominent, and growth pole effects are beginning to emerge. The spatial pattern evolves from scattered distribution to a multi-polar driven pattern, exhibiting pronounced unbalanced evolutionary characteristics. In terms of spatial association, ANQFPs exhibits a pronounced positive spatial autocorrelation, characterized by a spatial polarization pattern wherein high-value agglomerations coexist with low-value lock-ins. The geodetector test results indicate that economic fundamentals, industrial structure, technological innovation, green technology, and agricultural risk guarantee are the core stable driving factors for the spatial differentiation of ANQPFs.

documents.title: The Effect of Family Centered Empowerment Model based on Virtual Education to Improve on Strengthening the Family Role as DOTS Supervisor in Children with Pulmonary TB
documents.content:
Title: The Effect of Family Centered Empowerment Model based on Virtual Education to Improve on Strengthening the Family Role as DOTS Supervisor in Children with Pulmonary TB
Abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, particularly among children. Effective treatment adherence requires family involvement, where the role of Directly Observed Treatment Short-course (DOTS) supervisors is crucial. Innovative empowerment strategies are needed to strengthen family participation. This study aimed to examine the effect of the Family-Centered Empowerment Model (FCEM) based on virtual education to strengthen the role of families as DOTS supervisors for children with pulmonary TB. Methods: A quasi-experimental design with control and intervention groups was conducted. A total of 74 respondents were recruited using a total sampling approach. The intervention group received FCEM-based virtual education, while the control group received routine care. Data were collected using the FCEM questionnaire and analyzed with the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test and Mann–Whitney U test. Results: The results showed that elderly respondents predominated in both groups, accounting for 62.2% in the control group and 67.6% in the intervention group. In the control group, most families remained in the low category (64.9%), whereas in the intervention group, the majority shifted to the high category (75.7%). The findings confirmed a significant difference between the two groups after the FCEM based on virtual education intervention (p-value 0,011). Conclusion: It should not contain any references or displayed equations. The FCEM based on virtual education has more effectively strengthened the role of families as DOTS supervisors in children with pulmonary TB. This approach can be used as an innovative strategy to improve treatment success and accelerate progress toward TB elimination targets in Indonesia.

documents.title: Legal Model for Post-Flood Ecological Disaster Recovery in North Sumatra, Indonesia
documents.content:
Title: Legal Model for Post-Flood Ecological Disaster Recovery in North Sumatra, Indonesia
Abstract: This paper examines how corruption and environmental crimes committed by PT Toba Pulp Lestari have produced flash floods, ecological disasters, and the extinction of villages in Tapanuli, North Sumatra. Drawing on normative juridical analysis and case study of legal documents, court decisions, and civil society reports, it traces three mechanisms of corporate-state crime: financial corruption through transfer pricing and asset depreciation, environmental crimes through deforestation of 67,000 hectares of customary forest, and criminalization of Indigenous land defenders under the Job Creation Law. The article shows how law has been instrumentalized against Indigenous claims, creating what Nancy Fraser terms ‘abnormal justice’. In response, it proposes a legal action model comprising revocation of TPL’s concession through administrative courts, actio popularis for ecosystem recovery, and ratification of the Indigenous Peoples Bill. The analysis contributes a socio-legal framework for contesting corporate-state crime in Indonesia.
Authors: Marulak Pardede
Categories: Uncategorized

documents.title: PENERAPAN MODEL GROUP INVESTIGATION BERBANTUAN MEDIA DIORAMA UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KETERAMPILAN SOSIAL SISWA PADA PEMBELAJARAN IPAS
documents.content:
Title: PENERAPAN MODEL GROUP INVESTIGATION BERBANTUAN MEDIA DIORAMA UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KETERAMPILAN SOSIAL SISWA PADA PEMBELAJARAN IPAS
Abstract: This study was motivated by the low social skills of students, as indicated by their reluctance to accept randomly assigned groups, limited participation in group discussions, and lack of confidence in expressing their opinions. One effort to address this issue was the implementation of the group investigation learning model assisted by diorama media. Unlike previous studies that generally applied the group investigation model without concrete three-dimensional media, this study integrates diorama media as a means of encouraging direct physical interaction among students in IPAS learning. The purpose of this study was to improve students' social skills and learning outcomes in IPAS learning. The research employed Classroom Action Research (CAR) using the Kemmis and McTaggart model, which consists of four stages: planning, action, observation, and reflection. The study was conducted in two cycles involving 20 fourth-grade students of SDN 3 Nagrikaler, Purwakarta Regency. Data were collected through observation and tests. The results showed that students' social skills improved consistently from 67% in the pre-cycle, to 75% in cycle I, and reached 85% in cycle II. In line with that, students' learning completeness also increased from 55% in the pre-cycle, to 70% in cycle I, and reached 85% in cycle II. Based on these findings, the implementation of the group investigation learning model assisted by diorama media was proven effective in improving students' social skills and learning outcomes in IPAS learning. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya keterampilan sosial siswa yang terlihat dari adanya siswa yang menolak pembentukan kelompok secara acak, kurang aktif dalam kegiatan diskusi, serta belum berani mengemukakan pendapat. Salah satu upaya yang dapat dilakukan untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut adalah melalui penerapan model pembelajaran group investigation berbantuan media diorama. Berbeda dari penelitian sebelumnya yang umumnya menggunakan model group investigation tanpa media konkret tiga dimensi, penelitian ini mengintegrasikan media diorama sebagai sarana yang mendorong interaksi fisik antarsiswa secara langsung dalam pembelajaran IPAS. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan keterampilan sosial dan hasil belajar siswa pada pembelajaran IPAS. Metode yang digunakan adalah Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) dengan model Kemmis dan McTaggart yang meliputi tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan, observasi, dan refleksi. Penelitian dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus dengan subjek penelitian sebanyak 20 siswa kelas IV SDN 3 Nagrikaler, Kabupaten Purwakarta. Teknik pengumpulan data menggunakan observasi dan tes. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa keterampilan sosial siswa mengalami peningkatan secara konsisten dari 67% pada prasiklus, menjadi 75% pada siklus I, dan mencapai 85% pada siklus II. Sejalan dengan itu, ketuntasan hasil belajar siswa juga meningkat dari 55% pada prasiklus, menjadi 70% pada siklus I, dan mencapai 85% pada siklus II. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, penerapan model group investigation berbantuan media diorama terbukti dapat meningkatkan keterampilan sosial dan hasil belajar siswa pada pembelajaran IPAS.
Authors: Gandes Rahmi Mahayun Sari, Sofyan Iskandar, Tiara Yogiarni
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

documents.title: Conceptual model of the use of a local AI assistant based on large language models to prepare responses to the public appeals to medical institutions
documents.content:
Title: Conceptual model of the use of a local AI assistant based on large language models to prepare responses to the public appeals to medical institutions
Abstract: The paper is dedicated to the development of the conceptual model of the use of an assistant based on large language models to prepare responses to the public appeals to medical institutions. The key feature of the proposed approach is the intellectual system installing on a medical institution’s local server without transferring data to external services. This ensures compliance with the requirements of personal data protection and control of information flows. The article also discusses potential organizational effects, restrictions and risks of implementing this model in administrative practice of the medical institutions.

documents.title: Consensus-Based Pricing Model for Professional Services: A Legal and Technological Approach in Indonesia
documents.content:
Title: Consensus-Based Pricing Model for Professional Services: A Legal and Technological Approach in Indonesia
Abstract: The digital economy has significantly expanded professional service transactions in Indonesia; however, no established mechanism currently provides a reliable benchmark for determining fair service fees. This gap has contributed to price disparities, information asymmetry, and unequal bargaining power between service providers and clients. This study aims to examine the legal framework governing professional service pricing, assess the compatibility of a consensus-based pricing model with competition law principles, and develop a conceptual Consensus-Based Pricing Model. The study employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches. The findings demonstrate that the proposed model does not constitute price fixing, as it merely provides a transparent, non-binding, and informative pricing benchmark while preserving the parties' freedom to negotiate the final price. By leveraging digital platforms through a co-regulatory approach, the model has the potential to reduce information asymmetry, strengthen consumer protection and legal certainty, and promote fair market competition.

documents.title: Meningkatkan Keterampilan Berpikir Kritis, Pemecahan Masalah Dan Kolaborasi Matematika Menggunakan Model RAKAT Pada Siswa SD
documents.content:
Title: Meningkatkan Keterampilan Berpikir Kritis, Pemecahan Masalah Dan Kolaborasi Matematika Menggunakan Model RAKAT Pada Siswa SD
Abstract: Rendahnya keterampilan berpikir kritis, pemecahan masalah, kolaborasi, dan hasil belajar siswa kelas V SDN 1 Komet Banjarbaru dipengaruhi oleh pembelajaran yang masih berpusat pada guru dan kurang kontekstual. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan aktivitas guru dan siswa serta menganalisis peningkatan keterampilan berpikir kritis, pemecahan masalah, kolaborasi, dan hasil belajar melalui penerapan Model RAKAT yang mengintegrasikan Problem Based Learning (PBL), Realistic Mathematics Education (RME), dan Numbered Heads Together (NHT). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan dengan data kualitatif dan kuantitatif dalam jenis Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam tiga pertemuan pada 28 siswa kelas V. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, tes, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif kualitatif dan kuantitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa aktivitas guru mencapai kategori sangat baik, aktivitas siswa mencapai kategori sangat aktif, serta keterampilan berpikir kritis, pemecahan masalah, kolaborasi, dan hasil belajar pada ranah kognitif, afektif, dan psikomotor meningkat pada setiap pertemuan hingga ketuntasan belajar klasikal tercapai. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa Model RAKAT dapat menjadi alternatif pembelajaran inovatif untuk meningkatkan kualitas proses dan hasil pembelajaran matematika di sekolah dasar. Implikasi penelitian ini adalah Model RAKAT dapat digunakan sebagai acuan bagi guru sekolah dasar dalam merancang pembelajaran matematika yang lebih aktif, kontekstual, dan kolaboratif untuk mengembangkan keterampilan abad ke-21 siswa, serta menjadi referensi bagi penelitian selanjutnya mengenai pengembangan dan penerapan model pembelajaran terintegrasi pada konteks dan jenjang pendidikan yang berbeda.

documents.title: XÂY DỰNG MÔ HÌNH PHÒNG THỰC HÀNH PHÁP LUẬT SỐ TẠI TRƯỜNG ĐẠI HỌC TRƯNG VƯƠNG
documents.content:
Title: XÂY DỰNG MÔ HÌNH PHÒNG THỰC HÀNH PHÁP LUẬT SỐ TẠI TRƯỜNG ĐẠI HỌC TRƯNG VƯƠNG
Abstract: In the context of the ongoing digital transformation across all aspects of socioeconomic life, legal training at higher education institutions also needs to be reformed to meet the demands of the modern legal practice environment. This article focuses on analyzing the theoretical and practical basis of organizing legal practice activities in legal training, while clarifying the concept of a digital legal practice lab as a training model that integrates theory and practice on a technological platform. Based on an analysis of the development trends of legal activities in the digital environment, the article proposes two key operational models for digital legal practice labs: the online dispute resolution model and the online legal education and dissemination model. In addition, the article proposes several solutions for building and implementing a digital legal practice lab at Trung Vuong University, contributing to improving the effectiveness of legal practice training for law students in the context of digital transformation.
